methodological_rigor.justification: Design is appropriate for a first-in-human phase 1 trial: 3+3 dose escalation in parts A1/A2 and parallel disease-specific expansion cohorts with Bayesian stop rules. Eligibility, DLT grading (CTCAE v5.0), RECIST v1.1 imaging schedule, and five protocol amendments are clearly documented, and a data review committee provided oversight. Statistical analysis is appropriately descriptive with Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs for ORR and Kaplan-Meier for DOR/PFS, but the manuscript explicitly states no power or type I error calculations for part B, and biomarker cutoffs (CD8+, Treg, TGFB1) were determined empirically on only 14-16 ccRCC biopsies with no multiplicity correction. The single-arm design has no concurrent comparator, which is standard for phase 1 but constrains causal inference on ORR relative to anti-PD-1 retreatment; sex-based analyses were deferred due to small sample size.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single-arm, open-label, multicenter phase 1 first-in-human trial of a first-in-class selective anti-latent TGFB1 antibody - a non-randomized early-phase cohort study, placing it at Oxford 2b. Clinical relevance is high: it addresses the major unmet need of ICI resistance, and confirmed ORRs of 20.0% in heavily pretreated anti-PD-1-resistant ccRCC (including one CR, median DOR 10.6 months) with a 13.8-month median treatment duration are meaningful signals, especially given CONTACT-03/TiNivo-2 showed minimal benefit of ICI retreatment. Endpoints combine safety (patient-relevant) with surrogate efficacy (ORR, DOR, PFS), and the biomarker program (baseline Treg/TGFB1/CD8+) suggests a translational selection strategy that could inform the planned phase 2.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for an interventional trial, and the manuscript references a CONSORT diagram (Fig. 1), lists all 12 IRBs, cites NCT04291079 pre-registration, states adherence to ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki, and enumerates five protocol amendments. Primary/secondary/exploratory endpoints are pre-specified per protocol, and TRAEs and SAEs are reported by cohort with grades. Some CONSORT items are inherently limited by the single-arm, early-phase design (no randomization/blinding to report). A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary and online data/code availability statement are referenced but redacted in this blinded version; underlying patient-level data, biomarker raw data, and analytic code are not shown here, so reproducibility posture scores a 3.

novelty_literature.justification: Linavonkibart is presented as a first-in-class, fully human monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the latent form of TGFB1, sparing TGFB2/TGFB3 - a methodologically novel approach that targets the long-standing dose-limiting-toxicity problem that sunk pan-TGFB and TGFBR1 inhibitors (e.g., LY3022859, bintrafusp alfa cited as comparators). This is the first-in-human clinical readout for selective latent TGFB1 blockade, with mechanistic preclinical precedent (Martin 2020, ref 16) but no prior clinical data in this class. Novelty is primarily conceptual/translational rather than empirical paradigm-shift - the TGFB-ICI combination concept and biomarker candidates (CD8+, Treg, TGFB1) are themselves not new (Mariathasan 2018, Tauriello 2018). The positioning versus prior pan-TGFB programs and CONTACT-03/TiNivo-2 is credible and non-overclaiming.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical flow from mechanistic rationale through parts A1/A2/B results to biomarker correlates and discussion. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (ORR 20.0%/18.2%/9.1%/9.1% across cohorts, dosing schedules, n per part) and accurately reflects the paper. Acronyms (ccRCC, HNSCC, NSCLC, IMDC, MDSC, Treg, GARP, LTBP) are expanded appropriately, and figure/table captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, including a CONSORT diagram and swimmer/spider/waterfall plots for ccRCC. Minor issues: the eligibility section is dense and partially repeats between Methods and Results, and small-n biomarker claims (e.g., 57.1% ORR in Treg-high) could be more explicitly caveated in the abstract rather than only in Discussion.

key_strengths: First-in-human readout for a first-in-class selective anti-latent TGFB1 antibody that circumvents the cardiotoxicity that halted pan-TGFB and TGFBR1 inhibitors
Clinically meaningful 20.0% confirmed ORR (including one CR) and 13.8-month median treatment duration in heavily pretreated anti-PD-1-resistant ccRCC, benchmarked against CONTACT-03/TiNivo-2
Rigorous phase 1 architecture with 3+3 escalation, Bayesian expansion stop rules, DRC oversight, pre-registered NCT04291079, and clearly documented amendments
Paired longitudinal tumor biopsy and circulating biomarker program (CD8+, Treg, TGFB1, gMDSC) provides proof-of-mechanism and a candidate ccRCC selection strategy
Favorable safety profile largely overlapping pembrolizumab monotherapy with no CRS, no DLTs, and no treatment-related deaths
key_concerns: Single-arm design without concurrent comparator limits causal attribution of ORR to linavonkibart addition versus anti-PD-1 retreatment alone
Biomarker cutoffs for CD8+/Treg/TGFB1 were empirically determined on only 14-16 ccRCC biopsies with no multiplicity correction, risking overfit of the proposed selection strategy
Small per-cohort sample sizes in melanoma/HNSCC/urothelial (n=11 each) yield wide CIs around single-digit response counts
Part A1 excluded ccRCC, so monotherapy signal in the most responsive tumor type is untested
Data and code availability section is redacted in this version and patient-level/biomarker raw data are not visible for independent inspection
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound, mechanistically grounded first-in-human phase 1 of a first-in-class selective TGFB1 inhibitor with a clinically meaningful efficacy signal in anti-PD-1-resistant ccRCC and a coherent biomarker story places this at the top-tier oncology/translational-medicine range, pending minor refinements to the biomarker caveats and data-availability transparency.
